(ii) Main Points of Rutherford’s Atomic Model
1, Atom consists of positively charged central portion called nucleus.
2. Electrons are revolving around the nucleus with very high speed just
like the planets around the sun.
3. The size of the nucleus is very small as compared to the size of the
atom and most of the volume occupied by the atom is empty.
4. Atom is neutral. As the number of electrons is numerically equal to
that of protons.
5. Nucleus is responsible for mass and energy of the atom.

following defects.

1. Rutherford's atomic model is based on the laws of motion ang
gravitation, which are applicable to the neutral bodies and not on the
charged bodies.

2.1.2 Neil Bohr’ s Atomic Theory
In 1913, Neil Bohr presented a new atomic f
theory to overcome the defects of Rutherford's |
atomic model. Bohr considered hydrogen atom h
asamodel, This atomic model was based on the \~
following assumptions.
1, Electrons are revolving around the nucleus
in one of the fixed circular paths called shells
or orbits. Each orbit has a fixed energy. These 2
orbits are also called energy levels. 4

2. The energy of the electron in an orbit is?
proportional to its distance from the nucleus. * ~
The farther the electron from the nucleus, Neil Bohr
the higher will be the energy and vice versa.

3. As long as electrons are revolving around the nucleus in fixed circular
orbits, they do not gain or lose energy .i.e. energy of an orbit is fixed.

4. When an electron jumps from a higher energy orbit to the lower energy
orbit, it radiates energy and when it jumps from lower energy orbit to
higher energy orbit, it absorbs energy.
